newsitem.title: TAIWAN: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - July 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - July 21.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Taiwan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
CHINA TIMES - Two major parties fail to reach agreement on next phase of constitutional reforms.
President Lee Teng-hui to deliver speech to National Assembly.
UNITED DAILY NEWS - President Lee says abolishing provincial government not tantamount to declaring independence for Taiwan.
Oil price may fall in August.
LIBERTY TIMES - Opposition Democratic Progressive Party chairman Hsu Hsin-liang says bipartisan cabinet impossible in September reshuffle.
President Lee meets ex-U.S. senator and 1996 Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole.
COMMERCIAL TIMES - Electronic industry skyrockets in value following recent stock market gains.
United Microelectronics reportedly gave T$450 million signing bonus to new board member Don Brooks, former president of rival microchip maker Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.
ECONOMIC DAILY NEWS - President Lee tells Dole Taiwan cannot unite with communist China under "one country, two systems".
Opinions split on whether stock market daily movement ceiling should be scrapped.
